the server always assigns `source_kind=USER_DIRECT`/`user_confirmed=True` for this endpoint
(docs/adr/0010-...md "provenance / no source spoofing"); a public client can never choose its
own provenance metadata.

CareerProfileResponse.description:
A `User` with no `CareerProfile` row yet still gets a response here -- a virtual profile at
`profileVersion: 0` (docs/adr/0010-...md "profile creation"), never a 404. `createdAt`/
`updatedAt` are `null` only for that virtual case.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

FactStatus.description:
A fact's lifecycle state (docs/adr/0010-...md "retraction"). `ACTIVE` facts are the only
ones a default `TruthSnapshot` ever returns. `SUPERSEDED`/`RETRACTED` facts are never
hard-deleted -- they remain queryable for history/auditability.
FactStatus.title: FactStatus

FactType.description:
The canonical professional-claim categories WP1.2 must support
(docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md WP1.2 "Deliver"). `application_answer`-shaped facts are explicitly
out of scope here -- that concept belongs to the future `ApplicationAnswer` entity
(docs/DATA_MODEL.md), not this Truth Store.
FactType.title: FactType

FeedItemResponse.title: FeedItemResponse

FinalizeResumeImportCommand.description:
`decisions` must cover EVERY `PENDING` candidate of the target import, no more and no fewer
(docs/adr/0011-...md "review decisions": "no acceptance by omission") -- enforced in
`service.py` once the real pending set is known, not here. Each `candidateId` appearing at
most ONCE, and the list never exceeding `MAX_CANDIDATES_PER_IMPORT`, ARE enforced here, at the
command boundary itself -- round-1 independent review "Finding 4": a duplicate `candidateId`
(e.g. `[ACCEPT, REJECT]` for the SAME id) previously survived `service.py`'s own coverage check
unnoticed, because `{decision.candidate_id for decision in command.decisions}` is a set and
silently collapses duplicates -- the LAST decision for a duplicated id would win in the
dict-building loop while an EARLIER one may already have mutated `accepted_fact_candidates`,
risking a candidate whose own `review_state` ends up `rejected` while a `ProfileFact` was still
created from it. Rejecting duplicates here means `service.py` never needs to reason about this
case at all -- it is structurally unreachable once this command validates.
FinalizeResumeImportCommand.title: FinalizeResumeImportCommand

HardFilterId.description: The five canonical knock-out gates defined in ADR-0014.
HardFilterId.title: HardFilterId

HardFilterOutcome.description: Outcome classification for a hard-filter gate evaluation.
HardFilterOutcome.title: HardFilterOutcome

HeadlineCandidateValue.description:
The WP1.3-only top-level `headline` candidate shape -- never a `ProfileFact`, maps to
`CareerProfile.headline` instead (docs/adr/0011-...md "career profile top-level fields").
Carries its own `kind` so it can share ONE discriminated union with the nine `FactValue`
models below (round-1 independent review "Finding 5").
HeadlineCandidateValue.title: HeadlineCandidateValue

ImportFailureCode.description:
Normalized reason codes (docs/adr/0011-...md "error taxonomy") -- never a raw parser/library
exception message persisted or returned to a client.
ImportFailureCode.title: ImportFailureCode

ImportStatus.description:
Lifecycle of one resume import (docs/adr/0011-...md "import lifecycle"). `QUEUED` ->
`PROCESSING` is claimed atomically by the worker via a conditional `UPDATE` that ALSO matches
an already-`PROCESSING` row whose `processing_lease_expires_at` has passed -- a lease, not a
one-way latch (round-1 independent review "Finding 2"): a worker that crashes after claiming a
row leaves it reclaimable once the lease expires, rather than stuck in `PROCESSING` forever.
Redelivery of the SAME task while the lease is still active is never silently treated as a
no-op success -- it raises `ImportLeaseActiveError`, which the Celery task wrapper turns into
an explicit, bounded retry. `READY_FOR_REVIEW` -> `FINALIZED` is claimed the same way by
`finalize_resume_import` (a single-request, non-leased claim -- finalize has no long-running
work between claim and commit, so no lease is needed there), which is how two concurrent
finalize requests resolve to exactly one winner without a separate idempotency-key table.
ImportStatus.title: ImportStatus

(docs/adr/0010-...md "link safety"). No URL is ever fetched by this WP.
LinkFactValue.title: LinkFactValue

LocationPreferenceValue.description:
No geocoding, no coordinates (docs/adr/0010-...md "no geocoding in WP1.2") -- plain,
bounded, user-supplied location text.
LocationPreferenceValue.title: LocationPreferenceValue

ObservationStatus.description: Observation status for an individual job origin.
ObservationStatus.title: ObservationStatus

PreferenceFactValue.description:
`fact_type = preference`'s own payload is itself a discriminated union on
`preference_kind` -- one `FactType` member deliberately covers several preference shapes
(docs/adr/0010-...md "preferences"), since the canonical `fact_type` vocabulary
(docs/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md) names `preference` once, not once per kind.
PreferenceFactValue.title: PreferenceFactValue

ProfileFactResponse.description:
`value` is the SAME typed `FactValue` discriminated union the request side uses (round-2
independent review "BLOCKER 2") -- never `dict[str, object]`/`Record<string, unknown>` on the
generated TypeScript side. Pydantic validates the stored `value_json` dict against this union
on every construction, so a corrupted/incompatible DB row fails to build this response at all
(an unhandled 500, never a 200 with inconsistent data) rather than silently passing through
whatever bytes happened to be stored.
ProfileFactResponse.title: ProfileFactResponse

ProvenanceFieldSource.description: Origin category of a normalized field value.
ProvenanceFieldSource.title: ProvenanceFieldSource

ReplaceProfileFactRequest.description:
The replacement's `value` must match the ORIGINAL fact's `factType` -- enforced at the
service layer, not re-declared here (docs/adr/0010-...md "replacement model").
ReplaceProfileFactRequest.title: ReplaceProfileFactRequest

SalaryPreferenceValue.description:
Money is NEVER a float (docs/ENGINEERING_STANDARDS.md §11) -- integer minor units plus a
separate currency code, exactly `amountMinor`/`currency`'s documented shape. No currency
conversion ever happens here.

`currency` validates SHAPE only (three uppercase letters) -- NOT real ISO 4217 registry
membership. A well-formed but non-existent code (e.g. "ABC") is accepted (round-1 independent
review, "currency validation policy": implementing full registry validation would require a new
dependency this WP has no concrete need for; this is a deliberate, documented choice, not an
oversight).
SalaryPreferenceValue.title: SalaryPreferenceValue

SkillFactValue.description:
No proficiency is ever inferred -- `proficiency` only exists when the user actually
supplied one (docs/adr/0010-...md "no inferred proficiency").
SkillFactValue.title: SkillFactValue

SummaryCandidateValue.description: The WP1.3-only top-level `summary` candidate shape -- see `HeadlineCandidateValue`.
SummaryCandidateValue.title: SummaryCandidateValue

TruthSnapshotResponse.description:
The ONLY shape any future consumer (resume import review, matching, tailored resumes,
application answers, the Career Agent, WhatsApp) may use to ground generated external material
(docs/AI_AGENT.md §6, AGENTS.md §6) -- confirmed, active, non-retracted/superseded facts only
(docs/adr/0010-...md "truth snapshot filter").
TruthSnapshotResponse.title: TruthSnapshotResponse

UpdateCareerProfileRequest.description:
HTTP-specific wrapper over `CareerProfilePatchCommand` (round-3 independent review
"BLOCKER 1") -- adds `expectedProfileVersion` and camelCase wire aliasing only.
`headline`/`summary`/`target_roles`'s own validation (trim/non-blank/control-character
rejection/bounds/dedupe) and the "at least one mutable field" rule all live on the PARENT,
inherited here, not duplicated: `service.update_career_profile` requires the SAME
`CareerProfilePatchCommand` type directly, so a future channel adapter gets identical
validation without going through this HTTP class at all.

Optimistic-concurrency contract (docs/adr/0010-...md "optimistic concurrency"):
`expectedProfileVersion` must match the profile's current version or the request fails with
`PROFILE_VERSION_CONFLICT` (409) -- never a silent last-write-wins. Only fields actually present
in the request body are touched (`model_fields_set` distinguishes "absent" from "explicit
null"); the inherited `None` defaults exist only so a field CAN be omitted, not so sending it
always clears it.
UpdateCareerProfileRequest.title: UpdateCareerProfileRequest

UpdateJobAlertPreferenceRequest.description: Payload to update job alert preferences.
UpdateJobAlertPreferenceRequest.title: UpdateJobAlertPreferenceRequest

ValidationErrorItem.description:
One field-level validation failure. Carries only a normalized ``code`` (Pydantic's error
``type``) plus ``location``, never the raw ``input``/``ctx``/``msg``: those can echo request
data -- including personal data -- back into the error body.
ValidationErrorItem.title: ValidationErrorItem

WorkAuthorizationFactValue.description:
Sensitive/legal (docs/SECURITY_PRIVACY.md §5, docs/adr/0010-...md "work authorization"):
`answer` is a bounded string, never a bare unscoped boolean -- it only has meaning paired with
`jurisdiction`/`question_key`, and this WP invents no global legal-question catalog. The
server never infers or defaults this value; it is only ever written by an explicit, confirmed
user action (`service.py`'s `source_kind` enforcement).
WorkAuthorizationFactValue.title: WorkAuthorizationFactValue

YearMonth.description:
Year/month precision only -- never a fabricated day
(docs/adr/0010-...md "no invented date precision"). `month` absent means the user only knows
the year -- NEVER treated as January (or any other specific month) for comparison purposes
(round-2 independent review "BLOCKER 3": a prior `ordinal()` helper collapsed an unknown month
to January, which made e.g. `start=2024-12`/`end=2024` falsely register as "start after end" --
the user never asserted a January end, only a year).
YearMonth.title: YearMonth

post.description:
Resolves the caller's existing TapJob `User` for this verified Firebase identity, or creates
one (plus its `ExternalIdentity` link) if this is the first time this identity has ever
authenticated. Idempotent and concurrency-safe (`service.bootstrap_user`); never auto-links to
a different `User` based on email. The `ACCOUNT_CREATED` audit row (when `created`) commits in
the SAME transaction as the new `User`/`ExternalIdentity` rows -- never a separate, later
commit that could leave a `User` durably created with no corresponding audit row (2026
independent-review "account-created audit transaction").

post.description:
Revokes every Firebase refresh token for this account's linked identity (global, not
per-device -- docs/adr/0009-...md "per-device session revocation"). The audit row reflects the
ACTUAL provider outcome: a success row is written only after Firebase confirms the revocation,
and a failed provider call is recorded as a failure, never silently dropped
(docs/adr/0009-...md "audit transaction semantics"). Because `IdentityTokenVerifier` always
verifies with `check_revoked=True` (see `tapjob_api.identity.firebase`'s module docstring,
corrected 2026 independent-review finding 5), this backend rejects an already-issued ID token
on the very next request after this call, not merely after that token's own natural expiry --
the only thing that can lag is the CLIENT noticing (its local Firebase SDK session keeps using
its cached token until it next refreshes or itself observes revocation); this endpoint's own
server-side enforcement is immediate.
